chunks: Then God sent a raven which scratched the ground in order to show him how to hide the nakedness of his brother. "Alas, the woe," said he, "that I could not be even like the raven and hide the nakedness of my brother," and was filled with remorse.
ai.seo_question: How did God show Qabil how to bury his brother Habil?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from the first murder to the establishment of burial rites, emphasizing that Qabil’s remorse came after the act rather than preventing it. The raven serves as a divine teacher, illustrating the practical wisdom God instills in creation to guide humanity in honoring the dead. This narrative underscores the gravity of fratricide and the immediate, albeit belated, realization of guilt.
